answer: Invest in automation rather than hiring: covering peak by hiring needs about [F16] more pickers at roughly [F17] a year, while a [F8] system lifts capacity to about [F19] orders a day with today's team.
exec_summary: On-time shipping fell from [F1] to [F2] as daily orders grew from [F3] to [F4].
Today's team can pick about [F12] orders a day, a shortfall of [F13] before peak season begins.
At peak, demand of [F9] orders a day would need about [F16] extra pickers.
The system's one-time cost of [F8] is close to one year of the extra peak payroll at [F17].
situation: An online home-goods retailer picking all orders in its own warehouse with [F5] pickers.
complication: Orders grew to [F4] a day while capacity stayed near [F12], and on-time shipping fell to [F2].
key_question: Should the retailer hire more pickers or automate picking to ship on time through peak?
